title: The TEP Archive (August 2025 – September 2026): working records of the Terminal Equivalence Principle program, with Hecke eigenvalue tables, candidate Maass forms and numerical automorphy tests for the even icosahedral Artin representations of conductors 1951 and 2141
description:
The curated public record of the Terminal Equivalence Principle (TEP) research program, August 2025 – September 2026: roughly 800 primary documents, scripts and data files selected from a working corpus of 2,600+ files, with per-file SHA-256 hashes and provenance (CATALOG.csv, the 2026-08-05 catalog delta, and CATALOG_ADDENDUM_2026-07-25_to_2026-09-12.csv).

What the archive contains. (1) The information-geometric budget formalism and its tiered-rigor theorem notes; an experimental dictionary with its falsification record kept at full volume; a transmission-functor bridge from the budget to Langlands-type structures (2026-06/07). (2) The even-icosahedral campaign of 2026-07-27 – 2026-09-12: exact Hecke eigenvalue tables a_p = tr ρ(Frob_p) for p < 10^5 for the conductor-1951 and conductor-2141 even icosahedral Artin representations of Doud and Moore (J. Number Theory 118 (2006)), with the twist class fixed by a pre-registered sealed numerical selection and by an explicit Serre–Crespo spin-lift construction (65/65 agreement per conductor modulo one pre-declared quadratic character); the candidate Maass forms of eigenvalue 1/4 built from them; pointwise automorphy tests on complete generating sets of Γ_0(1951) (326 generators) and Γ_0(2141) (358), the Fricke constant identified with τ(χ)/(√N·a_N) to 10^-39, the adjoint L-functions passing their functional equation at 2^-53 with L(1, Ad ρ) to 30 digits, and a Heilbronn-type bound (a pole of L(s,ρ) of order m forces ord ζ ≥ 4m, ≥ 8m at real points, with an exact certificate); pre-registrations, sealed commitments, verification passes and same-day errata beside the records they correct. (3) The review ledger: assessments, adversarial passes, council records, and the program's own status and errata indices.

What is and is not claimed. The Artin conjecture for these representations is not claimed; entirety of the L-functions is not claimed; automorphy of the candidate forms is tested at finite precision and finitely many points, not proved. Searches on 2026-07-27, 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-12 (gaps disclosed in the records) found no prior numerical treatment of even icosahedral Maass forms or of these L-functions. No result in the archive has been re-run by anyone outside the collaboration that produced it. The framework (TEP) selected the objects; classical machinery realizes the results; the framework's standing as a physical theory is separately priced and open in the record. The deposit statement for the even-icosahedral objects is in the archive as a draft (20_records/cleanroom/cleanroom/STATEMENT_even_icosahedral_1951_2141_DRAFT_v2_for_countersign_20260912.md) and is offered, not yet countersigned.

Who wrote what. The program is William C. Lenchus's (the records address him as Will Copeland). The prose, code and computations were produced by Claude models (Anthropic) working at his direction in sessions whose records are preserved in full; the model is named in a record's header where recorded and otherwise attributed by the billing reconciliation of 2026-08-26. Internal verification was carried out by separate implementations within the same model family and is described as such, never as independent. See README.md, sections “Honest framing”, “Who wrote what” and “Countersign”.

Licensing. Documents, records, data tables and figures: CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE). Source code (50_code/ and all script files): MIT (LICENSE-MIT).

This version. Version 0.1.0 is a timestamping deposit of the working archive as of 2026-09-12, released before the deposit statement is countersigned. Version 1.0.0 of this record will be the one in which the statement is signed; a separate replication kit (tables, candidate forms, scripts, expected outputs) follows as a separate record with its own DOI.
notes: Timestamping deposit. Nothing in this archive has been refereed. The repository's README.md is the reading guide; CATALOG_ADDENDUM_2026-07-25_to_2026-09-12.csv carries SHA-256 and provenance per file for the September 2026 layer.
